content:
Apple has rolled out its latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models today, and alongside the new product launches, several of its Magic Keyboard accessories have also received minor updates.

The newest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels from the keys, replacing them with icons instead

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio have received powerful upgrades, featuring new chips including the next-generation M6 and the high-end M5 Ultra.

You can now pre-order the latest models: Mac mini here, and Mac Studio here.

In addition to the desktop computer improvements, Apple has also updated its Magic Keyboard lineup, with the new models featuring one subtle change.

The latest Magic Keyboard has removed the text labels from most keys, replacing them with icons.

Apple had previously adopted the same approach on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and the Magic Keyboard has now undergone the same change.

This update applies to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Commonly used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete have dropped their text labels and now display only icons. As for the extended model with a numeric keypad, keys like Home, Page Up, and Page Down have been given brand-new icons to replace the original text.

Aside from the switch to icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks identical to the previous generation overall, with full USB-C support, and the features and layout remain unchanged.

If you'd like to order the new Magic Keyboard through Amazon instead of Apple, you can get it here: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID version, and Touch ID with Numeric Keypad version (in black).

What are your thoughts on this change of removing text labels from the keys? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
